sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: Andrew Leland has always loved to read.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·利兰一直酷爱读书。

sentences.en: As a fifth grader, he was the kid who sat on a utility box during recess reading The Hobbit while everyone else played kickball.
sentences.zh: 上五年级时，当其他人都在玩踢球游戏时，他是那个坐在杂物箱上读《霍比特人》的孩子。

sentences.en: In middle school, he learned the trade names of the book imprints that published the druggie contemporary fiction that he was starting to get into.
sentences.zh: 在初中时，他记住了那些当时他刚开始接触的、出版瘾君子当代小说的图书品牌的商业名称。

sentences.en: And in 2003, he dropped out of college and moved to San Francisco to work for his favorite publisher, McSweeney's.
sentences.zh: 2003年，他从大学辍学，搬到了旧金山，为他最喜欢的出版商麦克斯威尼工作。

sentences.en: It was my dream job, and working there exacerbated my already intense fetish for print.
sentences.zh: 这是我梦寐以求的工作，在那里工作加剧了我原本就很强烈的纸质书情结。

sentences.en: I got to live out my fantasy of being an ink-stained wretch, even if that meant logging 12-hour days at an ink-less computer.
sentences.zh: 我得以实现我作为一名墨迹斑斑的穷酸文人的幻想，即使这意味着在一台没有墨水的电脑前工作12个小时。

sentences.en: I edited essays and interviews, laid out articles, and took a weird amount of pleasure in typographical minutia,
sentences.zh: 我编辑散文和采访，排版文章，并且对排版细节有着一种诡异的狂热，

sentences.en: like italicizing commas and rewriting headlines so they fit the frame just so.
sentences.zh: 比如给逗号打斜体，重写标题以便它们刚好塞进版面。

sentences.en: At McSweeney's, books and magazines were never just containers for words.
sentences.zh: 在麦克斯威尼，书籍和杂志从来不仅仅是文字的容器。

sentences.en: They were works of art unto themselves.
And I was trained to take as much care with the look and feel of the print as I did with the expression of the ideas in the text.
sentences.zh: 我受过训练，对印刷品的视觉和触感投入的关注，与我对文本中思想表达投入的关注一样多。

sentences.en: But as much as Andrew loved print, he still loves it, in fact,
sentences.zh: 但尽管安德鲁曾如此热爱纸质书，事实上他现在依然热爱，

sentences.en: he also has a condition that will eventually change his relationship to it pretty radically.
sentences.zh: 他也患有一种最终会彻底改变他与纸质书关系的疾病。

sentences.en: I'm going blind, really, really slowly.
sentences.zh: 我正在失明，非常、非常慢地失明。

sentences.en: Right now, it's like I've got a foot in both worlds, blind and sighted.
sentences.zh: 现在，感觉就像我一只脚踏在两个世界里，盲人与看得见的世界。

sentences.en: I have a degenerative retinal disease that's given me severe tunnel vision,
sentences.zh: 我患有视网膜退行性疾病，这导致了严重的管状视野，
所以基本上没有周边视野。

sentences.en: It's like I'm peering at the world through a toilet paper tube,
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我通过一个卫生纸卷筒在窥视世界，

sentences.en: one that gets a little narrower every few months.
sentences.zh: 这个筒每隔几个月就会变得更窄一点。

sentences.en: All right, I'm going to try to read this and then see if I got it right.
sentences.zh: 好的，我要试着读这个，然后看看我有没有读对。

sentences.en: My retinal specialist told me that I probably don't need to worry about losing the ability to read
sentences.zh: 我的视网膜专家告诉我，我可能不需要担心失去阅读能力，

sentences.en: for another five years or so,
but I've already started using a special digital program to learn Braille,
sentences.zh: 但我已经开始使用一个特殊的数字程序来学习盲文，

sentences.en: I want to get a jump start before I actually need it.
sentences.zh: 我想在真正需要之前抢先一步开始。

sentences.en: Can we recycle a metal can?
sentences.zh: 我们可以回收金属罐吗？

sentences.en: I know I'll still be able to experience books for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 我知道在我的余生中，我仍然能够体验书籍。

sentences.en: I'm lucky to be going blind in the digital age and the golden age of audio.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运能在数字时代和音频的黄金时代失明。

sentences.en: There's an abundance of well-produced audio books and technology
sentences.zh: 这里有大量的制作精良的有声读物和技术，

sentences.en: that can read aloud almost anything that appears on a screen.
sentences.zh: 它们可以大声朗读屏幕上几乎出现的任何内容。

sentences.en: My niece can ride a unicycle or two puzzles?
sentences.zh: 我侄女会骑独轮车还是拼两个拼图？

sentences.en: My niece can ride a unicycle or do puzzles.
sentences.zh: 我侄女会骑独轮车或拼拼图。

sentences.en: What the f*** does that mean?
My niece can do no such thing.
sentences.zh: 我侄女才不会做这种事。

sentences.en: But despite all that, there's still some mellow tragedy in the idea that in a few years,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，一想到几年后，

sentences.en: I'll probably no longer be able to read print.
sentences.zh: 我可能再也无法阅读印刷品，心中仍然带有一种淡淡的悲剧色彩。

sentences.en: After a life spent loving books, there's now a real urgency for me
sentences.zh: 在度过了热爱书籍的一生之后，盲人如何体验文学这个问题对我来说变得非常紧迫。

sentences.en: in the question of how blind people experience literature.
sentences.zh: 盲人如何体验文学这个问题对我来说变得非常紧迫。

sentences.en: I find myself deeply curious about what graphic design might mean to someone who can't see.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己对平面设计对于一个看不见的人来说意味着什么产生了深深的好奇。

sentences.en: And so I started looking into the history of reading technologies for the blind.
sentences.zh: 因此我开始研究盲人阅读技术的历史。
传统上，书籍是视觉对象。

sentences.en: And for centuries now, blind and sighted designers have been arguing over
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，盲人和明眼设计师一直在争论，

sentences.en: the most effective way to translate the visual ink print book
sentences.zh: 将视觉墨水印刷书转化为，

sentences.en: into an accessible form for people without sight.
sentences.zh: 适合无视力人群访问的形式的最有效方法是什么。

sentences.en: For as long as blind people have been reading,
there's been this tension between systems that try to stay close to the original form of a book
sentences.zh: 试图保持接近书籍原始形式的系统，

sentences.en: and systems that dramatically depart from our ideas of what a book can be.
sentences.zh: 与极大地背离我们对书籍可能性的看法的系统之间，就一直存在这种张力。

sentences.en: Sighted designers have made incredible breakthroughs
sentences.zh: 明眼设计师取得了令人难以置信的突破，

sentences.en: to create non-visual forms of reading for blind people.
sentences.zh: 为盲人创造了非视觉的阅读形式。

sentences.en: But, as one blind critic pointed out,
sentences.zh: 但是，正如一位盲人评论家所指出的，

sentences.en: sighted designers have a bad habit of, quote,
sentences.zh: 明眼设计师有一个坏习惯，引述一下，

sentences.en: talking to the fingers in the language of the eyes.
sentences.zh: 用眼睛的语言与手指对话。

sentences.en: So the history of blind reading is really the history of finding a new language
sentences.zh: 所以盲人阅读的历史实际上是为手指和耳朵寻找一种新语言的历史，

sentences.en: for the fingers and for the ears,
sentences.zh: 一种捕捉墨水印刷书基本要素的语言，

sentences.en: one that captures the essential elements of the ink print book,
sentences.zh: 但却是一种摆脱了视觉束缚的新语言。

sentences.en: but in a new language that's unbound from the visual.
sentences.zh: 但却是一种摆脱了视觉束缚的新语言。

sentences.en: And that history centers around two main shapes,
sentences.zh: 这段历史围绕着两个主要形状，

sentences.en: Our story starts in 18th century Europe,
sentences.zh: 我们的故事始于18世纪的欧洲，

sentences.en: before blind people were even taught to read at all.
sentences.zh: 在盲人甚至根本没有被教导阅读之前。

sentences.en: First off, no one thinks that it's possible for blind kids to learn.
sentences.zh: 首先，没有人认为盲童有可能学习。

sentences.en: the museum director at the American Printing House for the Blind in Louisville, Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 肯塔基州路易斯维尔美国盲人印刷厂的博物馆馆长。

sentences.en: And if they could, no one knows how to do it.
sentences.zh: 即使他们能学，也没有人知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: Without access to education, blind people were overwhelmingly poor,
sentences.zh: 由于无法接受教育，盲人绝大多数都很穷，

sentences.en: and their employment prospects were dim.
If their families had enough money and time to support them,
sentences.zh: 如果他们的家人有足够的金钱和时间来支持他们，

sentences.en: like adult children sitting idly around the house.
sentences.zh: 就像成年孩子一样闲坐在屋里。

sentences.en: Many others were forced to beg on the street.
sentences.zh: 许多其他人被迫流落街头乞讨。

sentences.en: There were a handful of institutions in Europe to support the poorest cases,
sentences.zh: 欧洲有少数机构支持最贫困的案例，

sentences.en: but they pitied the blind and hid them away from public view.
sentences.zh: 但他们怜悯盲人，把他们藏在公众视线之外。

sentences.en: But then this guy named Valentin Aoui comes along.
sentences.zh: 但随后一个名叫瓦朗坦·阿于伊的人出现了。

sentences.en: Aoui was born into a family of weavers in France,
sentences.zh: 阿于伊出生于法国的一个织工家庭，

sentences.en: and he was a skilled linguiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位熟练的语言学家。

sentences.en: He was first inspired to help the blind in 1771,
sentences.zh: 他最初受到启发去帮助盲人是在1771年，

sentences.en: where he saw a group of blind people being mocked during a street festival in Paris.
sentences.zh: 当时他在巴黎的一个街头节日上看到一群盲人被嘲笑。

sentences.en: They had been given dunce caps and giant fake glasses,
sentences.zh: 他们被戴上了傻瓜帽和巨大的假眼镜，

sentences.en: and they were made to play musical instruments and pretend to read books.
sentences.zh: 被迫演奏乐器并假装阅读书籍。

sentences.en: So Aoui founded the first known school for the blind.
sentences.zh: 于是阿于伊创立了第一所已知的盲人学校。

sentences.en: It was called the Royal Institute in Paris.
sentences.zh: 它被称为巴黎皇家研究所。

sentences.en: But even as he's getting the school going,
sentences.zh: 但即使在他创办这所学校的同时，
阿于伊还兼职着另一份工作。

sentences.en: And Aoui's side gig is as a translator for the king of France.
sentences.zh: 阿于伊的兼职工作是法国国王的翻译。

sentences.en: And so every now and then he'll get these fancy embossed invitations to various events.
sentences.zh: 所以他时不时会收到这些参加各种活动的精美浮雕邀请函。

sentences.en: And one day, one of Aoui's students, a kid named François Lassure, touched one of them.
sentences.zh: 一天，阿于伊的一个学生，一个叫弗朗索瓦·拉叙尔的孩子，摸了其中一张。

sentences.en: And François Lassure notices that he can feel something on these invitations.
sentences.zh: 弗朗索瓦·拉叙尔注意到他能感觉到这些邀请函上有东西。

sentences.en: And that gives Aoui the idea to develop this idea of embossed printing in raised letters.
sentences.zh: 这给了阿于伊开发这种凸版凸印印刷想法的灵感。

sentences.en: So in 1786, Aoui makes the first machine-embossed book for the blind,
sentences.zh: 于是在1786年，阿于伊制造了历史上第一台为盲人机器压印的书，
一本关于盲人教育的论文。

sentences.en: It's written in print, the kind that sighted readers would recognize.
sentences.zh: 它是用印刷体写的，明眼读者能认出的那种。

sentences.en: But the text is all raised so that blind students can feel the shape of the letters.
sentences.zh: 但文本都是凸起的，以便盲人学生能够摸出字母的形状。

sentences.en: Not just the first book for blind readers in history,
sentences.zh: 不仅是历史上第一本盲人读者书籍，

sentences.en: but basically the beginning of the idea that blind people can be educated.
sentences.zh: 而且基本上开启了盲人也可以受教育的理念。

sentences.en: But there are a few probleMs.
Well, first off, no one can afford to buy these books.
sentences.zh: 好吧，首先，没有人买得起这些书。

sentences.en: That's because the books are massive and prohibitively expensive.
sentences.zh: 这是因为这些书体积庞大且价格极其昂贵。

sentences.en: But they're also just really hard to read.
They're filled with ornate 18th-century letter forms,
sentences.zh: 它们充满了华丽的18世纪字母形式，

sentences.en: with their curly cues and flourishes, which are confusing to the fingertips.
sentences.zh: 带有卷曲的花饰，这让指尖感到困惑。

sentences.en: It's not until many years later, near the end of Aoui's life in 1821,
sentences.zh: 直到多年后，在1821年阿于伊生命快结束的时候，

sentences.en: that a very different blind reading system begins to develop.
sentences.zh: 一种截然不同的盲人阅读系统开始发展起来。

sentences.en: One that uses dots instead of lines.
sentences.zh: 一个用点代替线的系统。

sentences.en: It starts when a captain from Napoleon's army visits the school
sentences.zh: 它始于拿破仑军队的一位上尉访问学校，

sentences.en: to share a system that he'd developed for French soldiers.
sentences.zh: 分享他为法国士兵开发的一个系统。

sentences.en: The captain describes how the system allowed his men
sentences.zh: 这位上尉描述了该系统如何让他的部下

sentences.en: to silently communicate with each other on battlefields at night.
sentences.zh: 在夜间的战场上无声地互相交流。

sentences.en: This is a clip from a very lively educational movie about this history.
sentences.zh: 这是关于这段历史的一部非常生动的教育电影的片段。

sentences.en: Then I came up with the brilliant idea of making signs,
sentences.zh: 然后我想出了一个绝妙的主意，制作一些标志，

sentences.en: that my men could read in the dark merely by touch.
sentences.zh: 我的部下仅凭触觉就能在黑暗中阅读。

sentences.en: The director of the school at the time
led a group of students experiment with the embossed pages
sentences.zh: 带领一组学生尝试这位上尉留下的压印页面。

sentences.en: that the captain had left behind.
sentences.zh: 带领一组学生尝试这位上尉留下的压印页面。

sentences.en: And in that group was a 12-year-old blind kid named Louis Braille.
sentences.zh: 在那群人中有一个12岁的盲童叫路易·布莱叶。

sentences.en: he began to adapt that military code for blind people
sentences.zh: 他开始为盲人改编那个军事密码，

sentences.en: as an alternative to raised print.
sentences.zh: 作为凸版印刷的替代品。

sentences.en: Louis, you've been working on that for days.
sentences.zh: 路易，你已经研究这个好几天了。

sentences.en: So that all the letters of the alphabet
are represented by raised dots in different combinations.
sentences.zh: 都由不同组合的凸点来表示。

sentences.en: Louis Braille simplified the military code
sentences.zh: 路易·布莱叶简化了军事密码
并最大限度地提高了它的效率。

sentences.en: He substituted the 12-dot system developed by the captain
sentences.zh: 他将上尉开发的12点系统

sentences.en: which allowed blind people to read faster
sentences.zh: 这让盲人可以通过单指触摸识别字母，

sentences.en: by recognizing a letter with the touch of a single finger.
And while this code was inscrutable to sighted people,
sentences.zh: 虽然明眼人看不懂这个密码，

sentences.en: it was the system that blind people needed,
sentences.zh: 但它正是盲人所需要的系统，

sentences.en: designed by a blind person who understood intimately
sentences.zh: 由一个深入了解其内涵的盲人所设计。

sentences.en: the needs of those reading by touch.
sentences.zh: 满足那些通过触觉阅读的人的需求。

sentences.en: Another advocate for the blind would say of Braille,
sentences.zh: 另一位盲人权益倡导者曾这样评价布莱叶盲文：

sentences.en: it bears the stamp of genius,

sentences.zh: 就像罗马字母本身一样。

sentences.en: Braille didn't catch on right away.
sentences.zh: 布莱叶盲文并没有立即流行起来。

sentences.en: It wouldn't become the dominant system in France
sentences.zh: 它在法国并没有成为主导系统，

sentences.en: And it'd be nearly a century
sentences.zh: 而且几乎过了一个世纪，

sentences.en: before it became standard for blind readers in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它才在美国盲人读者中成为标准。
因为它实际上被压制了，
被一位善意且世界闻名的远见卓识者，
即盲人教育先驱所压制。

sentences.en: Around the same time that Braille was quietly developing

sentences.zh: 他的新阅读系统的大约同时，

sentences.en: an American named Samuel Gridley Howe
sentences.zh: 一个名叫塞缪尔·格里德利·豪的美国人

sentences.en: came to visit the Royal Institute in France.
sentences.zh: 来到法国皇家研究所参观。

sentences.en: He was doing research in anticipation
sentences.zh: 他当时正在进行研究，为

sentences.en: of opening the first school for the blind in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国开设第一所盲人学校做准备。

sentences.en: And I wish I could tell you that while in France,
sentences.zh: 我真希望我能告诉你，在法国期间，

sentences.en: Howe discovered the wonders of Braille.
sentences.zh: 豪发现了布莱叶盲文的奇妙之处。

sentences.en: But that's not how it went down.
Instead, he saw the raised letter books,
sentences.zh: 相反，他看到了凸字书籍，
但带有典型的美国风格，

sentences.en: he found all their fancy flourishes
sentences.zh: 他发现所有那些花哨的修饰

sentences.en: impractical and typical of European excess.
sentences.zh: 既不切实际，又带有欧洲式的过度奢华。

sentences.en: So he decided to make his own system
sentences.zh: 于是他决定制作自己的系统，

sentences.en: that improved on the Europeans' work.
And he came back and he modified it a bit.
sentences.zh: 他回来后对它进行了一些修改。

sentences.en: That's Kim Charlson, the director of the library

sentences.zh: 帕金斯学校图书馆的馆长，

sentences.en: which Howe established in Massachusetts in 1829.
sentences.zh: 该校由豪于1829年在马萨诸塞州建立。

sentences.en: Because they were using a more gothic-style font
sentences.zh: 因为他们使用的是一种更偏哥特风格的字体，

sentences.en: that he felt was a little too ornamental
sentences.zh: 他觉得这种字体装饰性太强，

sentences.en: and more difficult to read by touch.
sentences.zh: 通过触觉阅读会更困难。

sentences.en: So if one of Howe's French books
sentences.zh: 所以，如果豪的一本法文书

sentences.en: looked sort of like an ancient tome in a horror movie,
sentences.zh: 看起来有点像恐怖电影里的古代大部头，

sentences.en: whose letters rise up in fleshy protuberances,
sentences.zh: 上面布满了肉质突起般的字母，
那么豪的系统也很相似，

sentences.en: but it looks more runic, Tolkien-y, Elvish.
sentences.zh: 但它看起来更像卢恩文字、托尔金风格或精灵文。

sentences.en: Howe sharpened his letters' curves into points
sentences.zh: 豪把字母的曲线削尖成尖角，

sentences.en: to make them more distinct under the fingertips.
sentences.zh: 好让它们在指尖下更清晰可辨。

sentences.en: The letter O, for example, is shaped like a diamond.
sentences.zh: 例如，字母O的形状就像一个菱形。

sentences.en: Howe calls his new system Boston Line Type.
sentences.zh: 豪将他的新系统命名为波士顿线体。

sentences.en: Boston Line Type is really the beginning of literacy
sentences.zh: 波士顿线体确实是美国盲人

sentences.en: as we know it as a movement
sentences.zh: 我们所熟知的这场运动的

sentences.en: for people who are blind in the United States.
And like the older French system,
sentences.zh: 而且和较旧的法国系统一样，

sentences.en: Boston Line Type was designed to be read
sentences.zh: 波士顿线体的设计初衷是让

sentences.en: both by blind and sighted people.
sentences.zh: 盲人和明眼人都能阅读。

sentences.en: And if you're able to see and look at one of these books,
sentences.zh: 如果你能看见并看着这些书中的一本，

sentences.en: the letters are totally easily legible.
